payload.title: Does the concave engine work end-to-end?
payload.question: Do concave compound pieces run through the full pipeline (engine, runner, ledger, projections) producing valid, overlap-free packings, and does the convex control behave as in the parent project?
payload.hypothesis: All runs complete without error; every best legalised packing verifies overlap-free and contained by the independent checker; on the squ-in-squ n=6 convex control, harden's best legalised size is <= rigid's (the parent project found hardening wins on squares in a square). Concave instances are smoke runs only: no scientific claim is made from them here.
payload.decision_rule: Pass iff (a) zero run errors across all cells, (b) scripts/verify_packings.js reports zero pairwise overlaps (tolerance 1e-9) and full container containment on the best packing of every cell, and (c) the convex control holds: harden best_L <= rigid best_L on squ-in-squ n=6. Any failure is fixed in the engine, recorded as a plan amendment, and the campaign re-runs from scratch.

payload.title: Concave pilot: does hardening beat rigid starts on concave pieces?
payload.question: On three concave families at small n, does harden reach smaller containers than rigid starts at matched budget, and do the convex controls behave as in the parent project?
payload.hypothesis: Two-factor hypothesis: hardening beats rigid starts on concave families. (1) Path length: inscribed-disk share of piece area is ltri 6%, cross 31%, star5 41%, far below any convex piece (square 79%, triangle 61%, pentagon 86%), so the morph has far more room to work. (2) Hidden interlocking optima: concave optima require orientations a rigid search cannot easily reach. Positive control squ-in-squ (hardening wins in the parent project) should replicate; negative control tri-in-squ (tessellates) should tie or favour rigid.
payload.decision_rule: Descriptive pilot; no confirmatory claim. Report per-family harden vs rigid exact two-sided sign tests (best legalised size per instance, relative tol 1e-9). Proceed to C02 (pre-registered flagship: 48 seeds, frozen settings, harden/rigid/sa/pc) if (i) harden wins >= rigid losses on concave families overall, and (ii) the positive control replicates qualitatively (harden >= rigid on squ-in-squ). If harden is systematically worse everywhere including the positive control, the method params do not transfer to this codebase state: run a concave tuning campaign before C02 and record it as an amendment here.

payload.text: C01 concave pilot (1600 runs, 0 errors, 100/100 best packings verified overlap-free): the strong two-factor prediction is NOT supported. At tie tolerance 1e-4, concave harden vs rigid is 5 vs 5 with 7 ties (p=1); strict 1e-9 counts (7 vs 10) are inflated by 1e-6 legalization noise visible on squ-in-squ controls. The effect is instance-heterogeneous, not family-level: harden wins decisively on ltri n=5 (+0.61, 13%) and n=6 (+0.03), star5 n=7 (+0.011), n=8 (+0.033), n=9 (+0.10); rigid wins decisively on ltri n=7 (-0.27), n=8 (-0.10), cross n=5 (-0.33), n=8 (-0.18). Orientation variance of best rigid packings correlates only 0.27 with harden advantage - no clean geometric predictor emerges. harden crushes the classical baselines on concave: vs sa 19-6 (p=0.015), vs pc 24-1 (p=1.5e-6). Positive control (squ-in-squ) did not replicate the parent's n=11 signature at 16 seeds - likely a power issue (parent used 32 runs for a rare tilted-basin event), to be checked by a targeted replication.

payload.decision: Per the decision rule: (i) fails on strict counts (7 wins < 10 losses) and is a dead tie (5 vs 5) at noise-robust tolerance; (ii) positive control does not replicate at 16 seeds. payload.question: Does the generalized engine reproduce the parent's squ-in-squ n=11 signature, and what are fresh harden baselines on the handoff instances?

If replication fails, halt: do not interpret any handoff results until the engine difference is found. If it passes, the ltri n=5 and star5 n=9 harden runs supply the checkpoints for C02b-ltri and C02b-star5.

payload.title: Checkpoint handoff: ltri n=5
payload.question: Does rigid search reach harden's ltri n=5 pinwheel basin when started from a mid-morph checkpoint?
payload.hypothesis: On ltri-in-squ n=5, where harden beat rigid by 0.61 in C01, rigid search started from harden's tau~0.5 checkpoint reaches harden's basin (L≈4.0) while rigid from random starts does not. This is a mechanism test, not an efficiency test: the checkpoint cost a harden run, which is beside the point - the question is WHERE the search goes.
payload.decision_rule: Handoff succeeds iff rigid-from-checkpoint best-of-16 <= (C02a harden best on ltri n=5) + 1e-3 AND rigid-from-random best-of-16 > (C02a harden best) + 0.01. Success means the morph's contribution on this instance is basin delivery: rigid search reaches the pinwheel once started in its neighborhood but not from random starts. Failure (checkpoint cannot reach it either) means the late morph does essential work beyond basin delivery, or the checkpoint choice (tau~0.5) was wrong - either way the mechanism is not basin delivery alone.

payload.title: Morph-fraction ablation on ltri n=5
payload.question: How much of the morph path is needed to reach the ltri n=5 pinwheel basin?
payload.hypothesis: harden-half (tau0=0.5) reaches the ltri n=5 pinwheel (L<=4.001) but harden-quarter (tau0=0.25) does not: the basin is found in the first half of the morph, consistent with the tau~0.5 checkpoint handoff.
payload.decision_rule: Compare best-of-16 legalised sizes. If harden-half reaches <= 4.001 while harden-quarter does not (gap > 0.01), the basin is found in the first half of the morph. If both reach it, even a quarter-morph suffices and the critical interval is tau in [0, 0.25]. If neither reaches it, the full morph path is needed and the checkpoint result (tau~0.5) stands as the localization. Descriptive; feeds the mechanism story, no confirmatory claim.
